title: Kind to Those Younger Than Him
text: “Let us Class Up.”
“Bwee-hee.”

And so, in this manner, Ren’s companions proceeded with their Class Up. Incidentally, Itsuki’s companions were watching us with smug grins, apparently convinced that they couldn’t Class Up in the first place. This truly is the definition of ridiculous, I say.
“For the Class Up choices, prioritize agility.”

At this point in time, Ren was giving instructions based on his game knowledge. It vaguely reminded me of a loop where I’d stayed put in Melromarc. Come to think of it, the previous loop had been one after I’d already reconciled with Ren and Itsuki, once peace had settled in. And the one before that had been the loop where I reunited with Fleon-chan during the second wave. The spirit of the spear had flung me back to an earlier loop this time, and it felt rather nostalgic, indeed. Itsuki, too, was giving his companions instructions on where to Class Up. Well, Ren was one thing, but Itsuki’s companions were, without exception, hopeless cases. At best there was Riska, but she wasn’t around at this point in time. Utterly useless as a fighting force, I say.

When should I contact the Filolial Sage and arrange for Fleon-chan to be dispatched to Itsuki, I wondered. Well, since Itsuki from the previous loop had ordered—via Father—that I consider every possible measure other than Fleon-chan, I supposed I had no choice but to think it over, though it truly was a bother. As a last resort, I’d decided to hold off until he genuinely made a mistake. I’d aim for around the time of the Three Heroes Church incident. The rabbit man had already been engaging Itsuki in a war of words, so I’d let this one slide for now.

Now then, at this juncture, there was a method to plant distrust of the kingdom in Ren’s mind depending on whether or not he was permitted to Class Up. Since the rabbit man had already explained things, it stood to reason Ren had caught wind of it too.
“Well then, shall we prove here and now that we can’t Class Up?”
The rabbit man was asserting himself yet again. It seemed Itsuki’s attitude had genuinely gotten under his skin.
“Hmm, so you can Class Up. You… look like you’d be fast on your feet.”
It seemed Ren had judged based on the rabbit man’s ears. In truth, his stat growth was poor, and since he focused mainly on learning magic, his speed was actually somewhat questionable.
“Well, I suppose I could. I’ve got at least the minimum Level required.”
“Then the wave’s coming up soon too. Might as well get it done.”
“Kuro wants to do it too—Kuro wants to learn dark magic! Dark Saint Hero, grant darkness to these jet-black fangs and claws, Black Thunder!”

Ren glanced over toward Father again. Now that I thought of it, Kuro-chan apparently wanted to use dark-type magic. Black Thunder, otherwise known as Kurotarou, had wanted the same thing. But the story was that even Class Up hadn’t let him learn dark magic. Something to do with aptitude or bloodline seemed to be at play there. Luna-chan was a wielder of dark magic, though… it really was a complicated matter.
“Eh, can’t you just pick it?”
With a deep sigh, Ren gave in and answered Kuro-chan’s demand as if resigned to it.
“Yaaay.”
Kuro-chan trotted forward at Ren’s direction, ready to Class Up, but the members of the Three Heroes Church began muttering amongst themselves.
“Bwee bwee.”
“I already told you I gave permission. She’s apparently one of Motoyasu’s companions, and I’m telling you to let her.”
“Bwee bwee bwee.”
“Hey. What kind of nonsense are you spouting? Wasn’t it you lot who asked for this for the world’s sake?”
Even Ren was starting to look suspicious.
“Bwee… Dark Saint Hero, Kuro can’t do it?”

Kuro-chan asked Ren why she wasn’t being allowed to Class Up. With that innocent, friendly face turned toward him, Ren couldn’t bring himself to brush her off, and so he protested to the swine of the Three Heroes Church instead. Father had once remarked that Ren was probably the type who’d looked after his juniors. He apparently had a decent knack for taking care of those younger than him. Even when he seemed annoyed with someone, it didn’t mean he actually disliked them—that’s what Father told me afterward. Somehow, Ren and Kuro-chan just meshed well together. He did spend a lot of time around Kurotarou, otherwise known as Black Thunder, after all. Awakening to darkness, indeed.
“Bwee bwee, bwee-hee.”
“Money? You lot were the ones who said it wasn’t necessary since she’s a hero’s companion. In fact, my own companions got it for free, didn’t they?”
“B-bwee, bwee-hee.”
“A letter of introduction? Same thing. Don’t be ridiculous! Fine, I gave permission. That should count as the letter of introduction.”
“Bwee bwee bwee.”
Left to their own devices, the swine kept self-destructing, getting shot down by Ren one after another.

“Unless Naofumi apologizes to the king, you won’t allow it? How long are you going to hold a grudge over that farce? More importantly, it wasn’t Naofumi who gave permission—it was me. Naofumi has nothing to do with this.”
Hmm… things were unfolding rather differently than I’d expected.
“Or rather, that’s enough! What do you mean by cooking up some half-baked excuse like that!”
“That’s right! There was practically an attempted assault on his own daughter—of course he wouldn’t give permission!”
“Itsuki, that’s enough out of you too!”

Seeing Kuro-chan hang her head, Ren showed far more open emotion than I remembered from him and shouted at Itsuki. He seemed to be taking Kuro-chan’s side more than I’d expected. Now that I thought about it, I recalled Father once mentioning that Ren was kind to those younger than him. No doubt that part of him was responding to Kuro-chan.
“Motoyasu, Naofumi. Something’s off about this country… It’s almost like the king and the princess—the whole nation—are acting to persecute Naofumi, isn’t it?”
“Bwee-bwee! Bwee bwee bwee bwee!”

With Kuro-chan around, Ren arrived at the truth without even needing much prodding. Truly, interacting with Filolial-sama leads things in a better direction after all. This, too, was quite the discovery. Well, given this new possibility, I supposed it would be fine to tell him the truth. Depending on how things went, Itsuki might listen too.
“No… wait, Naofumi’s companion mentioned that Demi-Humans and Beastmen can’t Class Up. There’s something going on there.”

Ren immediately turned his gaze toward the rabbit man and Father. Father looked over at me, silently asking with his eyes what he should do. No problem at all, I say. Whatever happened now, the outcome would differ from before regardless. So I nodded.
“Whether you believe it is up to you, Ren… and Itsuki, but I’ll answer.”
“Bwee-bwee-hee! Bwee! Bweeeeeee!”
The swine tried to interrupt at an especially loud volume.
“Itsuki-sama! Lending your ear to the words of such a criminal—”
“Silence, I say.”
Swiftly, I unleashed a Silent Lance straight into the armored soldier standing behind Itsuki.
“Mald?! What are you doing!”
Itsuki instantly tried to enter combat stance, but Ren cut him off by pressing his sword to Itsuki’s throat.
“Listening to what Naofumi has to say before drawing weapons is what matters here. If there’s something these guys don’t want us hearing, that’s exactly why they tried to stop it.”
Ren had decent judgment in these sorts of matters, I’d give him that.
“Bwee—!?”
“I’d also like anyone who wishes to interrupt Iwatani-sama’s explanation to kindly keep quiet.”
Oh? The rabbit man had pressed a knife to a swine’s throat to silence her. The mongrel lizardman, too, seemed to be gathering strength, ready to fight at any moment.
“But surely such sudden actions cannot be permitted!”
“It’s not that long a story, is it? Just get to the point. Motoyasu, or anyone, really.”

“……This country, Melromarc, has a religion called the Three Heroes Church… and it’s decreed the Shield Hero and Demi-Humans and Beastmen as enemies. But if I’m discriminated against for no reason, the other heroes would grow suspicious and refuse to cooperate, and it’d cause friction with other nations. So—”
“You fabricated the crime, in other words. I see… well, whether it’s true or not has more or less been proven by these people here and by Itsuki’s own companions.”

“……There were nobles who tried to change relations with Demi-Humans and Beastmen, believing endless conflict would get us nowhere—but they died in the wave. And using that as an excuse, the people living on that noble’s territory were hunted down by the Three Heroes Church.”
The mongrel lizardman added this supplementary detail.
“Unbelievable. And this is supposed to save the world?”
“R-Ren-sama!”
One of Ren’s companions stepped forward, addressing Ren, who was visibly displeased.
“You too?”

“No, we intend to go with you, Ren-sama! At first, that’s all we thought, but traveling with you and seeing various places, we understood. Now isn’t the time to be saying such things. We believe the Shield Hero’s companions ought to be allowed to Class Up as well.”
Ren’s eyes carried a hint of suspicion still, but he sheathed the sword he’d drawn to restrain Itsuki. In turn, the rabbit man also put away his weapon.
